recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Hubble image archive. No published rating.

story: The brilliant core of NGC 1569 sparkles with light from millions of young stars in this Hubble image. At its center are giant star clusters sitting in a large cavity, with sculpted gas structures around them and two huge gas bubbles at left, floating like islands. The thousands of tiny white dots are stars in the galaxy's halo, and the biggest and brightest objects are foreground stars in the Milky Way.

Among galaxies in our local neighborhood, NGC 1569 is one of the most active, making stars 100 times faster than the Milky Way, at an almost continuous pace for the past 100 million years. Its central clusters each hold more than a million stars.

The cavity was blown out by massive young stars that already exploded as supernovae. Those blasts also drove a violent outflow of gas and particles that is carving giant structures, one of them, at lower right, about 3700 light-years long.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.75 x 1.66 arcminutes) and distance (11 million light years), the frame spans roughly 8,800 × 5,300 light-years. Its light set out about 11 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines data from Hubble's Wide Field Planetary Camera 2 and Advanced Camera for Surveys, including visible-light filters and narrow filters that isolate glowing hydrogen, nitrogen and oxygen. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: Narrow-band filters isolate the glow of particular gases, and Hubble's sharp view picks out individual halo stars as tiny white dots.

explore: The whole core is 5000 light-years wide. The largest bubble is about 378 light-years across and the smallest 119 light-years, lit by bright young stars inside them.

A new analysis puts the galaxy 11 million light-years away, farther than thought, in a group of about 10 galaxies centered on a spiral galaxy. Interactions there may be compressing its gas and sparking star birth.
alt: The bright core of a galaxy crowded with young stars, with a central cavity, sculpted gas structures, gas bubbles on the left and many tiny white dots around it.
